Create a Forest Plot with Multi-Prior Pooled-Effect Rows

Source: R/forest_sens_plot.R
forest_sens_plot.Rd

A classic forest plot – individual study rows exactly like bayes_forest() – whose "Pooled Effect" section shows one row per prior specification instead of a single pooled estimate, plus an (optional) prediction-interval row. Useful for showing how sensitive the pooled estimate is to the choice of prior directly on the same plot as the underlying studies. For a fuller sensitivity analysis comparing common- vs random-effects models, RoB exclusion, or RoBMA bias adjustment (but without individual study rows), see sensitivity_plot().

Usage

forest_sens_plot(
  model,
  data,
  measure,
  studyvar = NULL,
  yearvar = NULL,
  n_ctrl = NULL,
  n_int = NULL,
  event_ctrl = NULL,
  event_int = NULL,
  mean_ctrl = NULL,
  mean_int = NULL,
  sd_ctrl = NULL,
  sd_int = NULL,
  time_ctrl = NULL,
  time_int = NULL,
  sort_studies_by = "author",
  priors,
  prior_order = NULL,
  primary_prior = NULL,
  show_prediction = TRUE,
  study_output = c("density", "boxplot", "sq_whisker"),
  pooled_output = c("diamond", "density", "boxplot", "sq_whisker"),
  pred_output = c("diamond", "density", "boxplot", "sq_whisker"),
  label_control = "Control",
  label_intervention = "Intervention",
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  title_align = "left",
  xlim = NULL,
  x_breaks = NULL,
  x_label = NULL,
  null_value = NULL,
  add_rope = FALSE,
  rope_value = NULL,
  rope_color = "grey50",
  color_palette = NULL,
  color_study_posterior = "dodgerblue",
  color_study_posterior_outline = "blue",
  color_pooled_posterior = "blue",
  color_shrinkage_pointinterval = "purple",
  color_shrinkage_outline = "purple",
  color_shrinkage_fill = NULL,
  split_color_by_null = FALSE,
  color_favours_control = "firebrick",
  color_favours_intervention = "dodgerblue",
  add_arm_labels = TRUE,
  reverse_arm_labels = FALSE,
  color_pred_posterior = "orange",
  color_pred_outline = "darkorange2",
  plot_width = 4,
  font = NULL
)

Arguments

model

A fitted Bayesian meta-analysis model object. The study rows support the same backends as bayes_forest(): brmsfit, meta_stan, bayesmeta, stanreg, stanfit, CmdStanMCMC, bayesma, brma, rjags. Refitting under each entry in priors, however, only supports brmsfit, bayesmeta, meta_stan and brma (a single RoBMA::brma() fit, not a RoBMA::RoBMA() model-averaged ensemble) – other backends raise an error naming the unsupported model class. See bf_priors for which prior families each of those four backends can fit exactly.

data

A data frame containing the study data used for the meta-analysis.

measure

Character string specifying the effect measure. Must be one of: "OR", "HR", "RR", "IRR", "MD", or "SMD".

studyvar

Column name containing study identifiers/authors.

yearvar

Column name containing publication years. Default is NULL.

n_ctrl

Column name containing control group sample sizes.

n_int

Column name containing intervention group sample sizes.

event_ctrl

Column name containing control group event counts.

event_int

Column name containing intervention group event counts.

mean_ctrl

Column name containing control group means.

mean_int

Column name containing intervention group means.

sd_ctrl

Column name containing control group standard deviations.

sd_int

Column name containing intervention group standard deviations.

time_ctrl

Column name containing control group time periods.

time_int

Column name containing intervention group time periods.

sort_studies_by

Character string specifying how to sort studies. Options: "author" (default), "year", or "effect".

priors

A named list of prior specifications. Each element should be a list with name (display label), mu_prior (a bf_prior object), and optionally tau_prior (a bf_prior object). See bf_normal for constructors. Each prior is refit via the same machinery sensitivity_plot() uses, and shown as its own pooled-effect row labelled "name Prior".

prior_order

Optional character vector of prior keys specifying display order. Defaults to the order in priors.

primary_prior

Optional character key into priors. That prior's row label gets " (primary)" appended – use it to flag which prior specification matches the prior model was actually fit with.

show_prediction

Logical. Show a "Prediction interval" row below the priors (derived from model's own pooled estimate and tau). Automatically dropped (with a message) for common-effect models, which have no tau. Default TRUE.

study_output

Character string specifying how per-study rows are drawn: "sq_whisker" (default, matching a classic forest plot), "density", or "boxplot".

pooled_output

Character string specifying how each prior's row is drawn: "diamond" (default), "density", "boxplot", or "sq_whisker".

pred_output

Character string specifying how the prediction-interval row is drawn: "diamond" (default), "density", "boxplot", or "sq_whisker".

label_control

Character string for control group label. Default "Control".

label_intervention

Character string for intervention group label. Default "Intervention".

title

Character string for the plot title. Default NULL.

subtitle

Character string for the plot subtitle. Default NULL.

title_align

Character string specifying title alignment.

xlim

Numeric vector of length 2 specifying x-axis limits.

x_breaks

Numeric vector specifying custom x-axis break points.

x_label

Character string for the x-axis label. Default NULL (measure-specific label).

null_value

Numeric value specifying x-axis value of the null line.

add_rope

Logical indicating whether to add a ROPE. Default FALSE.

rope_value

Numeric vector of length 2 specifying ROPE range.

rope_color

Color for ROPE shading.

color_palette

Character vector of colors for the plot.

color_study_posterior

Color for study posterior densities.

color_study_posterior_outline

Color for study posterior outlines.

color_pooled_posterior

Fill color for each prior's row.

color_shrinkage_pointinterval

Color for shrinkage point intervals.

color_shrinkage_outline

Color for shrinkage plot outlines.

color_shrinkage_fill

Color for shrinkage plot fill.

split_color_by_null

Logical. Split posterior densities by null value.

color_favours_control

Colour for regions favouring control.

color_favours_intervention

Colour for regions favouring intervention.

add_arm_labels

Logical. Show "Favours Control/Intervention" labels.

reverse_arm_labels

Logical. Swap the arm label positions.

color_pred_posterior

Color for the prediction-interval row fill.

color_pred_outline

Color for the prediction-interval row outline.

plot_width

Numeric value specifying the relative width of the plot component. Default 4.

font

Character string specifying the font family.

Value

A patchwork object containing the complete forest plot.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
priors <- list(
  vague = list(
    name      = "Vague",
    mu_prior  = bf_normal(0, 10),
    tau_prior = bf_half_cauchy(0, 1)
  ),
  weakreg = list(
    name      = "Weakly Regularising",
    mu_prior  = bf_normal(0, 1),
    tau_prior = bf_half_cauchy(0, 0.5)
  ),
  informative = list(
    name      = "Informative",
    mu_prior  = bf_normal(0, 0.5),
    tau_prior = bf_half_cauchy(0, 0.3)
  )
)

forest_sens_plot(
  model         = fit,
  data          = dat,
  measure       = "OR",
  studyvar      = Author,
  n_ctrl        = N_Control,
  n_int         = N_Intervention,
  event_ctrl    = Event_Control,
  event_int     = Event_Intervention,
  priors        = priors,
  primary_prior = "weakreg"
)
} # }
